findings.title: (1) listActiveMembers — full quote, and the :118-127 throw claim
(2) Query shape — entu_user is NOT in either roster-load request; a per-person fetch is required
findings.detail:
Two Entu requests make up today's roster load, and neither projects `entu_user`:

- `listActiveMembers` (rosterData.ts:102-108) queries the MEMBER entity: `entity?_type.string=member&status.string=active&props=person,_parent&limit=500` — props `person`, `_parent` only.
- `listProfilesForPerson` (rosterData.ts:164-170) delegates verbatim to `listMyProfiles` (src/lib/profile/profileData.ts:156-198), which queries `profile`-typed CHILD entities of the person: `entity?_type.string=profile&_parent.reference=${personId}&props=name,email,_sharing&limit=10` — props `name`, `email`, `_sharing` only.

`entu_user` lives on the PERSON entity, not on `member` or `profile`, and every existing call site in this codebase reads it via a single-entity GET keyed by personId: `entity/${personId}?props=entu_user` — src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:379 (inside `mintSelfLinkInvite`) and identically at src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:53 (`readOwnLinkedIdentities`, reading the CALLER's own person). Neither of today's two roster-load queries touches `entu_user` or this prop-def at all.

Answer to the central question: surfacing redemption state on the roster requires an ADDITIONAL fetch beyond what `loadRoster`/`loadRosterWithRealNames` already issue — one GET per row's `personId` in the shape `entity/${personId}?props=entu_user`, parsed the way `mintSelfLinkInvite` already parses it (inviteData.ts:388-390): `{ entity?: { entu_user?: Array<{ _id: string; uid?: string; provider?: string; email?: string; invite?: string }> } }` (the `StoredEntuUserEntry` shape, inviteData.ts:355-362). There is no bulk-list precedent for this property anywhere in the repo — both existing call sites key by one specific personId, not a `props=entu_user&limit=N` list across many persons. [unverified — that entu-api itself has no bulk variant is inferred from this repo's absence of one, not checked against entu-api docs directly.] Building #294 therefore means fanning out one additional per-member entu_user read, most naturally mirroring the existing `Promise.all` profile fan-out `loadRoster` already does (rosterData.ts:347-352).

findings.title: (3) RosterRow — full type, every field
(4) Roster page row rendering — file:line, and where a badge attaches
linkedIdentities.ts quoted in full (main, not the live pipeline branch)
(a) 'caller's own person only' is a CALL-SITE convention, not a code-level restriction
findings.detail: The header comment (linkedIdentities.ts:3-5) and the function docstring (:41-44, 'the caller's OWN bound auth identities') assert own-person scope. But the function signature itself (`listLinkedIdentities(cfg, personId, fetchImpl)`, :46-50) takes an arbitrary `personId` string with no internal check that `personId` matches any identity derived from `cfg.token` — nothing in the function body ties `personId` to the caller. Both real call sites happen to pass the caller's own id: `src/routes/profile/+page.svelte:328` (`listLinkedIdentities(cfg, personId, ...)` where `personId = current.personId`, sourced from the authenticated session/route-load context at :393, `+page.svelte:393`) and `src/routes/auth/callback/run-link-callback.ts:131-135` (`listLinkedIdentities({db: invite.db, token: result.token}, linkPersonId, fetch)` — `linkPersonId` is `state.linkPersonId`, the initiating/authenticated person, per the file's own header comment at run-link-callback.ts:1-13). So: (a) is TRUE as documented *contract and observed usage*, but FALSE as a code-enforced guarantee — the real gate is Entu's server-side rights resolution on `cfg.token` against whatever `personId` is supplied, not anything in this file.

findings.title: (b) The '***' mask replaces only the invite-token FIELD's value, not the whole entry
findings.detail: linkedIdentities.ts:37: `/** Masked as '***' — presence alone marks an un-redeemed invite placeholder. */` documents the `invite?: string` field on `StoredEntuUserEntry` (:32-39). Per the header comment (:8-10, citing entu-api utils/entity.js:594-598 [unverified — entu-api source not read this turn]), Entu's server masks JUST the bearer-token string that would otherwise sit in `invite`, replacing it with the literal `'***'`. The rest of the placeholder entry is NOT masked to a sentinel — `_id` comes back as the real property id, and `uid`/`provider`/`email` are simply ABSENT (undefined) on a placeholder entry, not present-but-masked. So masking is field-scoped (one string value), not entry-scoped or object-scoped.

findings.title: (c) Return shape for redeemed vs un-redeemed diverges further than the wire shape — placeholders are collapsed to a bare count
findings.detail: Redeemed/bound entry (`entry.invite` not a string, :67) → pushed into `identities: LinkedIdentity[]` as `{_id, uid: entry.uid ?? '', provider: entry.provider ?? '', email: entry.email ?? ''}` (:71-76) — full 4-field object, per-entry `_id` preserved. Un-redeemed placeholder entry (`typeof entry.invite === 'string'`, :67-70) → NOT turned into any identity-shaped object at all; it only increments `pendingInvites` (:68) and its `_id` is discarded — `continue`s past the push. So the module's public return contract (`LinkedIdentitiesResult` at :27-30) is strictly coarser than the raw Entu wire shape: it throws away the placeholder's `_id` (which `mintSelfLinkInvite`'s stale-cleanup step needs to call `DELETE property/{_id}` — inviteData.ts:401-408) and reduces N placeholders to a single integer.

findings.title: To read another member's redemption state: same call shape, different personId + caller's own token — but listLinkedIdentities' reduced shape is NOT directly reusable for #294's three-state render
findings.detail:
Syntactically the call is unchanged: `listLinkedIdentities(cfg, targetPersonId, fetchImpl)` where `cfg.token` is the READING caller's own JWT (e.g. an admin/roster-viewer) and `targetPersonId` is the OTHER member's person id — nothing blocks this today (see finding on (a)). Whether it succeeds server-side is a rights question, not a code question: entuFetch (:51-57) sends `cfg.token` as the Authorization bearer against `entity/${personId}?props=entu_user`, and Entu resolves visibility from that token against the target entity's rights, independent of who `personId` names.

Per issue #294 (gh issue view 294, PO:Gama comments) this was live-probed on polyphony 2026-09-08 and recorded in `scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-294-gap-a-b-rights-level-live-2026-09-08T10-28-03-167Z.json` (read via `git show main:...`, confirmed present on main): a root-equivalent caller read both a placeholder-state person and a bound-state person in full (`gap-a-state-unredeemed`, `gap-a-state-redeemed` steps); separately, a caller holding ONLY `_viewer` on the target (`gap-b-_viewer-grant`/`gap-b-_viewer-read` steps) also got the private `entu_user` property back in full — but that `_viewer` test ran ONLY against the PLACEHOLDER-state person (`targetId: 6a9fe33020ebf490c690a829`, the same id as the earlier `gap-a-state-unredeemed` fixture) and the probe explicitly stopped there (`gap-b-early-stop`, reason: 'positive result — further escalation adds no new information'). So `_viewer` sufficiency for the BOUND/redeemed shape specifically was never directly re-probed at `_viewer` — only inferred from the separate, higher-privilege probe result plus the general finding 'property-level sharing does not filter a rights-holding reader.' [speculative: whether an ordinary member's `_viewer` grant, if narrower in some undiscovered way, reads bound entries identically to placeholder entries — not independently tested.]

Does any EXISTING function already do a person-by-id `entu_user` read? YES, two: (1) `listLinkedIdentities` itself (linkedIdentities.ts:46-57) — generic over `personId` as shown above, though its RETURN shape collapses placeholders to a count and drops their `_id` (see prior finding), so it can tell you 'is bound' (an entry lands in `identities`) but NOT the placeholder-vs-absent distinction with the `_id` needed for `reinvite`/`withdraw` (which operate on `property/{_id}` — inviteData.ts:401-408). (2) `mintSelfLinkInvite`'s internal read step (`src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:371-397`) — same `entity/${personId}?props=entu_user` GET, generic over `personId`, but it's a private first step of a mint-and-sweep function, not exported as a standalone reader, and it's documented (inviteData.ts:364-369) as operating on 'the caller's OWN person.'

Neither existing function returns the raw three-state discriminable shape (`uid` present / `invite` present without `uid` / key absent) that issue #294 needs per roster row. The nearest existing PRECEDENT for how #294 would be built is `rosterData.ts`'s `listProfilesForPerson` (rosterData.ts:164-169) — documented at rosterData.ts:15-17 as 'a thin, same-file wrapper around the ALREADY-generic `listMyProfiles(cfg, personId, ...)`', called per member in `loadRoster`'s `Promise.all` fan-out (rosterData.ts:349, `listProfilesForPerson(cfg, member.personId, fetchImpl)`) under the roster-viewing caller's own `cfg.token`. #294 would most naturally follow this exact template — a new thin per-person `entu_user` reader (reusing `entuFetch`'s `entity/${personId}?props=entu_user` GET, or reusing `listLinkedIdentities`'s underlying fetch but NOT its lossy reduction) fanned out per `ActiveMember.personId` from `listActiveMembers` (rosterData.ts:87-142).

findings.title: createInvite (inviteData.ts:166-320, main) — full quote, ordering, and why it cannot invite an existing member
findings.detail:
Verified against `git show main:src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts` (workspace-app, main — NOT the live pipeline branch). Full function quoted in my working notes; key excerpts by line:

- Signature at line 166 matches the issue's `:166` citation exactly: `export async function createInvite(cfg: EntuCfg, input: CreateInviteInput, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): Promise<CreateInviteResult>`.
- Ordering is exactly person-create -> self-`_editor` grant -> member-create, sequentially, no branching:
  - Person create: lines 193-238 (`personProps` at 201-206, POST `entity` at 207-217, `_id` apparent-success guard at 232-237).
  - Invite-token extraction: lines 240-250 (comment: 'the ONLY guaranteed read of the token').
  - Self-`_editor` grant: lines 252-271, comment 'parity with entu-api's native auto-create tail ... load-bearing for T4.6 lazy creates'.
  - Member create: lines 273-317 (`memberProps` at 285-291, POST at 292-302).
- CANNOT invite an existing member — structurally, not just by convention: `CreateInviteInput` (line 59-61) has exactly one field, `dbEntityId` (the target collective). There is no person-id, email, or member-id input anywhere in the function, and no read/lookup step against any existing person or member before the person-create POST at line 207 (the comment at 176 even states 'All reads precede all writes' and the only reads are `resolveTypeId` x2 and `resolvePersonParentId` — none of which look up an existing person). Every call unconditionally mints a brand-new person entity (line 207) and a brand-new member entity (line 292). Confirmed at the call site too: `src/lib/components/admin/InviteSurface.svelte` (main) calls `createInvite({ db: dbId, token }, { dbEntityId })` (line 242) and has no email/person/member input field anywhere in the component (grepped for 'email'/'person' — only unrelated hits: 'person-scoped org resolution' comment, and `createError.personId`, which is the id of the person orphaned on a mid-sequence failure, not an invite target).

findings.title: Redemption binds the CLICKER, not the intended recipient — verified in both entu-api source and mvox-app's redeem.ts
No existing re-send/re-mint path for an already-invited or already-member person; what a new one must do/avoid
findings.detail:
Plainly: NO such path exists today. `createInvite` (see finding 1) can only mint for a brand-new person — pointing it at an existing member/person is not just unsupported, it structurally cannot happen since it takes no person-targeting input at all. The only OTHER mint function in the codebase, `mintSelfLinkInvite` (`src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:371-463`), mints on an EXISTING person by id — but its sole call site is `src/routes/profile/+page.svelte:659`: `const { inviteToken } = await mintSelfLinkInvite(ctx.cfg, ctx.personId);`, where `ctx.personId` is the currently signed-in user's OWN person (this is the 'link a second OAuth provider to my own account' self-service flow, #193/#219 — not an admin-facing re-invite-someone-else feature). Grep confirms these are the only two call sites in `src`.

What a new admin-facing re-send/re-mint feature would have to DO (all load-bearing, per inviteData.ts's own comments on `mintSelfLinkInvite`, lines 322-463):
1. Read the target person's `entu_user` property array first (identity-read phase, mirrors lines 377-393).
2. Sweep and DELETE every stale un-redeemed `invite`-carrying entry BEFORE minting a new one (lines 398-415) — because `findStoredInvite` in entu-api (`routes/auth/index.get.js:270-275`) does `entity?.private?.entu_user?.find((u) => u.invite) || null`, i.e. takes the FIRST matching entry. Leaving an old placeholder in place means a fresh mint's own token can end up practically un-discoverable/inconsistent at redemption time (this is inviteData.ts's own documented 'Hazard 2: orphan accumulation', lines 333-338).
3. Then POST the mint trigger to `entity/{personId}` (the UPDATE endpoint, not entity-create) with body `[{ type: 'entu_user', string: INVITE_MINT_TRIGGER }]` (pattern at lines 419-429) to get a fresh token back in the response (masked to `***` on every later GET).
4. Require the calling admin to hold effective `_editor`/`_owner` rights on that specific person entity — a 403 there means 'the person lacks self-_editor' in the self-link case (lines 431-439); for an ADMIN acting on someone ELSE's person, whether the admin's own rights reach that person depends on whatever rights chain the target person actually has (its `_inheritrights: true` plus its `_parent` = the database entity, per `createInvite` lines 201-206) — I did NOT verify live whether an admin's database-level grant cascades to an arbitrary invited person's entity, so treat 'admin already has the rights to do this' as [unverified]/[speculative], not assumed.

What it must AVOID:
- Must NOT touch a bound identity: any `entu_user` entry carrying `uid` is real and must never be deleted/overwritten (explicit in the Hazard-2 comment, lines 337-338, and structurally distinct from the `invite`-only placeholder shape per the issue's own probe).
- Must NOT call `createInvite` against an existing member — that mints a SECOND, competing person+member pair rather than re-sending anything (finding 1).
- Must NOT assume minting is idempotent/replacing (see finding 4) — an un-swept second mint leaves two placeholder rows.

findings.title: Where invite links are minted, and minting a second link does NOT invalidate the first (verified, not assumed)
findings.detail:
Two mint sites, both in `src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts` (main):
1. `createInvite` — mints via entity CREATE (`POST entity`, lines 207-217), for a brand-new person only, called from `InviteSurface.svelte:242` (admin 'invite a new member' UI).
2. `mintSelfLinkInvite` — mints via entity UPDATE (`POST entity/{personId}`, lines 419-429), for an EXISTING person (the caller's own), called from `profile/+page.svelte:659` ('link another provider' self-service UI).

Does a second mint invalidate the first? NO — verified from entu-api source, not assumed:
- The mint operation (`utils/entity.js:462-467`, both create and update paths route through the same `insertProperties`/property-append logic) is a property INSERT keyed on the trigger literal, not a targeted overwrite of a prior invite property. mvox-app's own code says this explicitly: inviteData.ts comment lines 328-331, 'the mint trigger fires on the entity UPDATE endpoint too ... APPEND is platform-level: a fresh entu_user value never disturbs an existing bound identity' — and by the same append mechanics, never disturbs an existing UN-redeemed invite placeholder either, which is exactly why `mintSelfLinkInvite` has to manually DELETE stale placeholders itself (lines 398-415) before minting — dead code if a second mint already invalidated the first.
- On the redemption side, entu-api's `findStoredInvite` (`routes/auth/index.get.js:270-275`) does NOT match on the specific token value presented at redemption at all — it looks up `entityId` from the decoded token and returns the FIRST `entu_user` entry on that person carrying ANY `invite` value. `jwt.verify(query.invite, jwtSecret)` (line 206) only checks that the presented token's own signature/expiry are valid; it never cross-checks that this token is 'the current' stored one. So an OLDER unexpired token, if its placeholder property is still present, remains independently redeemable even after a newer mint — the newer mint neither revokes the JWT nor deletes the older stored placeholder.
- Net effect: two un-redeemed placeholders can coexist on one person after two mints without an explicit cleanup step; both of their tokens verify independently until 7-day (source) / measured-24h-live (per #23's comment thread, 'minted invite-token lifetime measured 24h live vs the pinned-source 7d') expiry. This is precisely the 'orphan accumulation' hazard inviteData.ts documents by name (lines 333-338) as the reason `mintSelfLinkInvite` sweeps stale placeholders first.

findings.title: Test runner confirmed: vitest only, no Playwright (research finding still holds on main)
findings.detail: package.json (origin/main) — `"test": "vitest run"` (line 13), `"test:watch": "vitest"` (line 14), `"vitest": "^4.1.10"` devDependency (line 39). No `playwright` anywhere in package.json, no playwright config file in the tree (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -i playwright` → empty). vitest.config.ts / vite.config.ts are the only test-relevant config files. #287's research conclusion holds unchanged.

findings.title: RosterRow has NO join/identity field today — every page.roster*.spec.ts inlines RosterRow literals, none can express an un-redeemed member
findings.detail: `RosterRow` (src/lib/roster/rosterData.ts:174-210, origin/main) has memberId, personId, name, email, sectionIds?, dbEntityId?, profileName? — no entu_user/uid/invite/join-state field of any kind. No dedicated fixture-builder module for roster rows exists (`git ls-tree -r origin/main -- src | grep -iE 'fixture|testHelpers'` scoped to roster → empty) — every one of the ~15 `page.roster-*.spec.ts` files inlines `RosterRow` object literals by hand, e.g. page.roster.spec.ts:129-130 (`{ memberId: 'member-1', personId: 'person-a', name: 'Ada Lovelace', email: 'ada@example.com' }`), :241, :256. None carry any identity/invite field, so none can express 'placeholder' or 'bound' today. Two ways this gets fixed: (a) widen `RosterRow` with a new field and touch every inline literal across those ~15 files plus the 9 `toEqual<RosterRow>`/`toEqual<RosterRow[]>` sites in the data-layer specs listed below [speculative — a design choice, not observed], or (b) keep RosterRow untouched and have the row snippet issue a SEPARATE per-row read (e.g. reusing `listLinkedIdentities`), in which case existing RosterRow literals need no change but each page spec needs a new mock/fixture for that separate call.

findings.title: 9+ strict toEqual<RosterRow>/<ActiveMember> assertions in the data-layer specs would need updating if RosterRow/ActiveMember gains a populated field
findings.detail: rosterData.spec.ts (origin/main) uses `toEqual<RosterRow>({...})` at lines 202, 218, 232, 252, 262, 289, 300 and `toEqual<RosterRow[]>([...])` at 358, 396; `toEqual<ActiveMember[]>([...])` at 66, 89, 112. rosterData.database.spec.ts:42-49 has a full `toEqual([{memberId,personId,sectionIds,dbEntityId}])`. rosterData.realNames.spec.ts has full-row `toEqual([...])` at 164, 203, 269, 332, 400, 427, 454. Vitest's `toEqual` ignores keys whose value is `undefined`, so these only break if a new field is actually populated (non-undefined) in the row/member the test constructs — not merely declared on the type. Since `entu_user` lives on the PERSON entity, not the member entity, `listActiveMembers`'s wire shape (rosterData.ts:98-147, pinned by the exact `props=person,_parent` substring check at rosterData.spec.ts:122, and by ghostFree.spec.ts:26-28's `status.string=active`/`_type.string=member` checks) is very likely unaffected by #294 — the join-state read is necessarily a separate per-person fetch. [speculative: depends on the eventual implementation's shape.]

findings.title: Structural sole-mechanism guard (singleInviteMechanism.spec.ts) will fail on any new source file that contains the substring 'entu_user' unless exempted
findings.detail: src/lib/invite/singleInviteMechanism.spec.ts walks every non-spec `.ts`/`.svelte` file under `src/lib` and `src/routes` (via `findSourceFiles`, src/lib/testing/soleLiteralGuard.ts:29-40) and fails (`isSoleCreatePathViolation`, soleLiteralGuard.ts:15-25) if the literal substring `entu_user` appears in a file that isn't `.spec.ts` and isn't in `MINT_EXEMPT` (singleInviteMechanism.spec.ts:26: currently `['lib/invite/inviteData.ts', 'lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts']`). This is load-bearing for #294: any new roster-row read of `entu_user` — a new module, an inline fetch URL in `+page.svelte`, or a widened `listActiveMembers` query string — trips this guard unless that file is added to `MINT_EXEMPT` (editing the spec itself) OR the read is routed through the already-exempt `listLinkedIdentities` (src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:46-80).

findings.title: listLinkedIdentities already computes exactly the three-state discriminator, generically over personId — reuse avoids the structural-guard problem
findings.detail: src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:46-80 (`listLinkedIdentities(cfg, personId, fetchImpl?)`) issues `GET entity/{personId}?props=entu_user` and returns `{identities: LinkedIdentity[], pendingInvites: number}`, discriminating on `entry.invite` presence (linkedIdentities.ts:67-77) exactly as the probe specified: identities.length>0 → bound, pendingInvites>0 → placeholder, both zero → absent. Its own spec (linkedIdentities.spec.ts:53-84) already pins this exact three-way split with a full-shape `toEqual`. Despite the doc comment saying 'the caller's OWN person', nothing in the code or its test restricts `personId` to the caller (PERSON_ID='person-me' is just the fixture's chosen id) — it is call-site-generic, matching `listProfilesForPerson`'s established pattern of reusing a self-scoped-looking function for an arbitrary personId (rosterData.ts:164-170's own doc makes the same move). [speculative: whether the eventual implementation actually reuses this function is a design choice outside this task's scope, but it is the only exempt, already-built reader that returns a distinguishable three-state shape.] Callers today: src/routes/auth/callback/run-link-callback.ts and src/routes/profile/+page.svelte only.

findings.title: Every page.roster-*.spec.ts mocks $lib/roster/rosterData at the function level, not the wire — new join-state data must arrive via the loadRosterWithRealNames mock's resolved RosterRow[], not via fetch stubbing
findings.detail: Confirmed by grep across all 15 page.roster-*.spec.ts + page.roster.spec.ts (origin/main): each has `vi.mock('$lib/roster/rosterData', () => ({ loadRosterWithRealNames: loadRosterMock }))` (e.g. page.roster.spec.ts:46, page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts:58, page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:79, page.roster-arrange.spec.ts:85, page.roster-indent.spec.ts:124, page.roster-picker.spec.ts:43, page.roster-sections.spec.ts:40, page.roster-sections-live-wire.spec.ts:38, page.roster-create-section.spec.ts:46, page.roster-empty-remove.spec.ts:63, page.roster-damaged-parent.spec.ts:60). None of these mock fetchImpl/global.fetch for row data — two files (page.roster-damaged-parent.spec.ts:137, page.roster-sections-live-wire.spec.ts:143) DO `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)`, but that stub is scoped to the unrelated section-list query (`_type.string=section`), a red herring for #294. Consequence: if the join-state is baked into `RosterRow` (option (a) above), a new state reaches these page tests simply by adding fields to the `loadRosterMock.mockResolvedValue([...])` literal — no new wire mocking needed. If instead the page issues a SEPARATE per-row fetch (option (b), e.g. reusing `listLinkedIdentities`), each page spec needs either a new `vi.mock('$lib/profile/linkedIdentities', ...)` (following the pattern already used in page.profile-linked-accounts.spec.ts:176) or a `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)` keyed on the entu_user URL (following the page.roster-damaged-parent.spec.ts:125-136 stubGlobalFetch pattern).

findings.title: Two page.roster*.spec.ts files already mock $lib/invite/inviteData wholesale — full caller/importer map
findings.detail: page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts:69-73 and page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:110-113 both do `vi.mock('$lib/invite/inviteData', async (importActual) => ({...await importActual(), createInvite: createInviteMock, mintSelfLinkInvite: mintSelfLinkInviteMock}))` as a REGRESSION GUARD, not because the roster page currently calls either function (confirmed: `grep -n "inviteData\|invite" src/routes/roster/+page.svelte` on main returns nothing — the roster page imports neither today). page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts:404-416 (test titled 'reinstate is ONE action: calls reinstateMember for her, mints NO invitation, and refreshes both lists') asserts `expect(createInviteMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` and `expect(mintSelfLinkInviteMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` after clicking reinstate — this must keep passing once #294's invite/reinvite/withdraw controls land on the same page (reinstate must still never mint). Full non-spec importer map (origin/main): `listActiveMembers` — rosterData.ts:346, routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:503, routes/library/+page.svelte:935,1254. `loadRoster` — rosterData.ts:396 (loadRosterWithRealNames), routes/+page.svelte:518,2179, routes/admin/+page.svelte:272, routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:1570. `loadRosterWithRealNames` — routes/roster/+page.svelte:187 only. `toRosterRow` — rosterData.ts:350, memberLifecycle.ts:178. `mintSelfLinkInvite` — routes/profile/+page.svelte:659 only. `createInvite` — src/lib/components/admin/InviteSurface.svelte:242 only. `listLinkedIdentities` — routes/auth/callback/run-link-callback.ts, routes/profile/+page.svelte only.

findings.title: withdraw's mechanism already exists verbatim inside mintSelfLinkInvite — sweep-without-mint
findings.detail: src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:371-463 (`mintSelfLinkInvite`): step 1 reads `entity/{personId}?props=entu_user` (:377-393), step 2 filters entries where `typeof e.invite === 'string' && e.invite.length > 0` and DELETEs each via `property/{stale._id}` sequentially, aborting on the first failed DELETE with a named `SelfLinkMintError` (:394-415, phase `stale-invite-cleanup`) — a bound identity (carries `uid`, never `invite`) is excluded by that same filter and is never touched. This is exactly the mechanism the PO comments (issue #294) describe as `withdraw`'s required behavior ('all-or-report', 'a bound identity is never touched'). No spec currently exercises steps 1-2 in isolation (without the mint) — inviteData.spec.ts and selfLink.spec.ts test the full mint flow only; extracting/reusing the sweep for a standalone `withdraw` is new test surface, not covered by any existing assertion.

findings.title: Row-rendering insertion point identified: the memberRow snippet, admin-gated block
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3212-3251 (origin/main) — the `{#snippet memberRow(row: RosterRow, showSection: boolean)}` block renders `roster-row-name`/`roster-row-email`/`roster-row-section` spans unconditionally, then an `{#if admin === 'admin'}` block (3227) containing the existing record-edit pencil (no self-row exclusion, per its own comment at 3228-3232) and, further down, a separately-gated deactivate/reinstate block that DOES exclude the admin's own row [not fully re-verified here, referenced by rosterData self-row exclusion comment near the deactivate handlers]. This is the natural site for the three-state badge + invite/reinvite/withdraw controls; whether it goes in the pencil's `admin==='admin'` block or needs its own self-row exclusion (an admin can't invite/withdraw herself, presumably) is a design decision outside this task's mechanical scope. [speculative on exact placement/gating — not something the current source decides.]

findings.title: MULTI-COLLECTIVE: entu_user is per-collective, not per-person globally — redemption state does not travel across collectives
findings.detail: Verified from source, not assumed. `entu_user` lives on the Entu `person` entity (src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:24, src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:4-9), and a person entity is scoped to exactly one collective: `resolvePersonParentId` sets the invited person's `_parent` to the collective's own database-root entity (inviteData.ts:73-99), and `resolveDatabaseEntityId` queries `entity?_type.string=database&limit=1` — 'exactly one per db' (inviteData.ts:112-118). Collective identity is confirmed 1:1 with the Entu db name: `Collective.db` is 'the Entu db name' and `Collective.personId` is 'the user's person-id WITHIN THIS COLLECTIVE'S db' (src/lib/collectives/types.ts:1-11), sourced per-db from the JWT's `accounts` map. So a human who belongs to two collectives has two independent `person` entities in two independent databases, each with its own independent `entu_user` array — a member bound (joined) in collective A can legitimately be absent or an unredeemed placeholder in collective B, because collective B's admin runs a wholly separate `createInvite` against a wholly separate database. The roster's own per-row read of redemption state must be re-fetched fresh on every collective switch and must never be cached/keyed only by `personId` across collectives (personId values are not even comparable across dbs). This is exactly the class of bug #287 (the sibling pipeline touching this same file) is fixing for other roster state: `routeLoad`'s `reset({isSwitch})` callback (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:116-166) already exists specifically to null out every piece of per-row/per-collective transient UI state (`pendingDeactivateId`, `deactivateRefusal`, `recordEditorMemberId`, `showInactive`, `inactiveRows`, etc.) on a collective switch — any new invite/reinvite/withdraw armed-confirm state or in-flight-mint state must be added to that same reset block or it will leak across a switch, reproducing the #287 bug class for the new feature.

findings.title: LOCALES: naming convention, bundle locations, and reusable invite keys
findings.detail: Four flat JSON bundles at repo root: messages/en.json, messages/et.json, messages/lv.json, messages/uk.json — verified byte-parity: each holds exactly 594 keys, 82 of them `roster_*`, 17 `admin_invite_*` (checked on `main`). Roster keys follow a strict `roster_<subject>_<action_or_state>` convention, e.g. `roster_member_deactivate`, `roster_member_deactivate_confirm_prompt` / `_confirm` / `_cancel`, `roster_member_deactivate_failed`, `roster_member_reinstate`, `roster_member_reinstate_failed` (messages/en.json:219-230) — this is the established precedent for a two-step armed-confirm control (deactivate) and its failure copy, directly reusable in shape for `withdraw`'s confirm step. A wholly separate, already-shipped `admin_invite_*` family exists for the standalone 'Invite a new member' admin page (messages/en.json:59-75): `admin_invite_submit`, `admin_invite_link_label`, `admin_invite_copy`/`admin_invite_copied`, `admin_invite_bearer_warning` ('Anyone who opens this link can claim this membership — it is a bearer secret...'), `admin_invite_show_once`, `admin_invite_error`, `admin_invite_copy_error`. These are strong reuse candidates for the new roster row invite/reinvite controls (same underlying mint mechanism, same bearer-secret risk) rather than duplicating new strings — in particular the bearer-secret warning and copy-link/copied pair. A third family, `invite_landing_*`/`invite_error_*` (messages/en.json:47-58), is scoped to the unauthenticated invite-redemption landing page and is not relevant to admin-facing roster copy. No key already exists for a three-state badge label or a `withdraw`/`reinvite` roster action — those are genuinely new and should follow the `roster_member_*` naming pattern (e.g. `roster_member_invite_state_*`, `roster_member_reinvite`, `roster_member_withdraw`) to sit alongside the deactivate/reinstate family they most resemble.

findings.title: RIGHTS TIERS: /roster requires only an authenticated session; every mutating control on the page is admin-gated as a whole-block pattern, badge-visibility doesn't have precedent for a split read/write gate here
findings.detail: The roster route itself is protected only by session presence — `isProtectedPath` (src/lib/auth/guard.ts:42-47) has no admin distinction; any authenticated collective member reaches /roster. Every mutating surface on the page is then gated behind `{#if admin === 'admin'}` as a single fail-closed check: the record-edit pencil block (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3227), section create/reorder/remove/rename (3378, 3627, 3854, 4444), deactivate (3429, admin-only AND never on the viewer's own row: `row.personId !== selected?.personId`), and — notably — the entire 'inactive members' panel including its reveal toggle (4567: `{#if admin === 'admin' && status === 'ready'}`). `admin` comes from `adminStore`/`resolveAdmin` (src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:32-40+), which reads rights off the collective's single database-root entity (#161 ruling) and is fail-closed on every non-'admin' state ('loading'/'error'/'not-admin' all deny). Given the issue #294 probe's finding that a `_viewer`-level read already returns the three-state `entu_user` shape (no admin rights needed to READ it), there is a genuine, currently-unresolved design tension for the build: today's established codebase pattern for 'extra state about a member beyond the base roster' (the inactive panel) is to gate the WHOLE feature — visibility and control together — behind `admin === 'admin'`, not to split a viewer-visible badge from an admin-only control. The issue thread frames it as a build decision (badge could be shown to all; invite/reinvite/withdraw controls should stay admin-gated per the existing whole-page pattern), but no comment or code on `main` actually decides whether the badge itself is member-visible or admin-only — that choice is open and should be made explicit rather than defaulted by copy-pasting the inactive-panel's whole-block gate. [speculative: I did not find any ruling in the issue thread that explicitly states the badge must be visible to non-admin members; Mihkel's scope comment only specifies 'per roster row' render the three states and admin-gate `reinvite`/`withdraw`, without addressing who besides admins sees the badge.]

findings.title: PROVENANCE: nothing in the schema distinguishes invite-created from other persons — and today there is no 'other' path, so the discriminator is provenance-agnostic by construction
findings.detail: `createInvite` (src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts) is verifiably the ONLY code path in this app that creates a `member` entity — confirmed by grep: `memberTypeId`/the member `_type` POST occurs nowhere else in src/. So every row currently on the roster came from an admin invite, and its person started in the placeholder state (entu_user carries the mint-trigger literal at create, inviteData.ts:201-206) before potentially being redeemed. Native Entu auto-provision (routes/auth/index.get.js, entu-api, not this repo) is a separate, out-of-band person-creation path referenced only in comments (inviteData.ts:5, :253, :433) — mvox-app's own code never calls it and has no member-creation flow tied to it. Issue #294's thread explicitly considered and REJECTED adding a provenance marker (the 'inverted marker' proposal) after a live probe showed it solves a problem that doesn't exist: the three-state read of `entu_user`'s contents (uid vs invite vs absent) is deliberately the sole, provenance-agnostic discriminator — 'Read `person.entu_user` per roster row and render the three states... discriminating on the entry's contents, never on the property's presence' (Mihkel/Gama DECISION comment, issue #294). So: no, nothing distinguishes invite-created vs. other persons today, and per the ruling nothing should — the three-state discriminator is defined to behave identically regardless of how the person entity came to exist. `linkedIdentities.ts` (src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:31-38) already implements and types this exact parse (`StoredEntuUserEntry` with optional `uid`/`invite`) for the profile page's own-identity read, and `mintSelfLinkInvite` (src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:355-393) already implements the same discrimination for its stale-placeholder sweep — both are directly reusable rather than re-derived for the roster badge/controls.

findings.title: A11Y: existing badge/pill idiom and live-region conventions to follow
findings.detail: The codebase already has a small-pill/state-badge idiom to match rather than invent: `event/[id]/+page.svelte:2266,2275` renders `rounded-full border px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[9px] tracking-wide uppercase {eventTypeBadgeClass(...)}` — a text pill whose color class comes from a per-state lookup function; `library/+page.svelte:1379` uses a plain color-dot lookup table, `REPERTOIRE_BADGE_DOT_CLASS[repStatus] ?? 'bg-ink-4'`; `library/+page.svelte:1533/1536` uses a text pill (`rounded-full bg-ink-5 px-2 py-0.5 text-ink-2`) for availability state. A three-state invite badge should follow this same shape (lookup-table CSS class keyed by state, not ad hoc conditionals), and its concrete insertion point on the roster page is the `memberRow` snippet (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3212), immediately beside the existing `data-testid="roster-row-name"` (3219) and `data-testid="roster-row-email"` (3220) spans — a new `data-testid="roster-row-invite-state"`-style span would match the file's existing `roster-row-*` testid convention. For live-region conventions: the page's established pattern is per-purpose SEPARATE `role="status" aria-live="polite" class="sr-only"` regions mounted once at page level for success/progress narration (e.g. `data-testid="roster-reorder-status"` at 3611, similarly for reorder/rename/record-save), paired with INLINE `role="alert"` elements placed next to the specific control/row on failure (e.g. `data-testid="section-remove-error"` at 3758, `data-testid="roster-record-save-error"` at 3353) — never a single shared alert region for unrelated actions. A `reinvite`/`withdraw` action pair would need its own dedicated `role="status"` success region (mirroring the deactivate/reinstate and record-save precedents) plus an inline `role="alert"` on the acting row for failure, consistent with the file's stated rule that a role="alert" appears 'because it appears after the [action]' (comment at 3416-3420) rather than being present-but-empty at load.

findings.title: 1. The body's three Mihkel-questions — status
findings.detail:
Q1 'Which state did you see?' — ANSWERED. Mihkel, 2026-09-08: "Persons with entu_user vs persons without" (comment 'The state to render is a THREE-state field'). This is Finding-3's redemption state (entu_user contents), NOT Finding-1's person-less state — Gama's comment states this explicitly: 'That settles question 1: it is redemption state, not the missing-person case.'

Q2 'Admin visibility of redemption state is a rights decision' — ANSWERED, and resolved as NOT a blocker. Live probe (2026-09-08, polyphony, cited in-repo at scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-294-gap-a-b-rights-level-live-2026-09-08T10-28-03-167Z.json, referenced by comment): 'a caller holding entity-level rights reads the _sharing: private entu_user in full.' Final comment adds: 'The _viewer-level read returned the placeholder shape too, so the render does not depend on the caller being an admin.' The body's premise that this 'gates the whole feature' is superseded, not merely answered.

Q3 'Re-send existing link or mint a second?' — ANSWERED. Final comment (product rule, not literally Mihkel-quoted but posted (*PO:Gama*), whom memory records as trusted PO proxy): 'never two live links. One person, at most one redeemable link, at any moment... withdraw-then-mint in one action.' The DECISION comment separately confirms the mechanism: 'reinvite reuses mintSelfLinkInvite's contract: sweep stale placeholders, then mint.'

All three original questions are answered; none is open as stated in the body.

findings.title: 2. States that CAN vs CANNOT exist in a loaded roster today — from code
findings.detail:
CANNOT exist as a rendered row: 'no person' (Finding 1's state). rosterData.ts:118-127 (main): if `raw.person?.[0]?.reference` is falsy, listActiveMembers THROWS ('cannot read person reference...'), and the throw is unconditional per-member inside the whole-list .map() — one bad member fails the ENTIRE roster load, not just that row. So this state, if it existed, would never appear as a visible row with an [invite] control; it would take down the page. Reinforced by Finding 2: inviteData.ts:166-290 (createInvite, main) is the app's SOLE member-create path (per the module's own header comment: 'Structurally enforced sole path') and it always creates person→member together in one sequence — the app itself can never produce a person-less member. Such a member could only arise from a non-app write (migration/seed/manual Entu edit), and the issue body notes 'crede's roster loads today' as evidence none currently exists there [unverified — live data state, not checkable from source].

CAN exist (assuming a loadable roster, i.e. every row has a readable person): all three entu_user states are real. 'bound' (uid present) and 'placeholder' (invite present, no uid) are both normal, expected, reachable via createInvite→redemption. 'absent' (no entu_user key at all) is reachable ONLY the same way Finding-1's state is — a person created outside createInvite — because inviteData.ts:197-201 (main) shows createInvite's person-create POST unconditionally includes `{ type: 'entu_user', string: INVITE_MINT_TRIGGER }`, so every app-created person starts in 'placeholder', never 'absent'. So the DECISION's 'missing' state and Finding-1's 'no person' state share the same root cause (non-app-created data) even though they are mechanically different fields (member.person vs person.entu_user).

findings.title: 3a. Remaining decisions — product (need Gama/PO)
findings.detail:
Concrete, short list — everything else in the thread that changes the build is already ruled:

(i) None found as strictly open at product-authority level for the SCOPE already decided. The DECISION comment ('#294 proceeds... Scope, settled') and the follow-up decision ('ready — sequencing is dev's call') together cover state model, controls-per-state, collapse-on-withdraw, and one-live-link invariant. I could not find an unresolved product question in the thread as it stands.

(ii) The one item that is PO-adjacent but explicitly NOT this issue's decision: whether to file the viewer-level `_sharing:private` platform finding as a follow-up issue ('File the followup if required' — Mihkel). Not a #294 build decision; flag only if the team wants to actually file it.

If the PO wants something to rule on, the honest answer is: nothing blocks scope. What remains is engineering (below).

findings.title: 3b. Remaining decisions — engineering (ours to make, listed for completeness)
findings.detail:
(i) WRITE-side rights for reinvite/withdraw are UNPROBED. The probe (comment 'PROBE RESULT: readable') tested only a READ (GET .../entity/{id}?props=entu_user) at admin and _viewer levels. mintSelfLinkInvite (inviteData.ts:371-461, main) — the function reinvite is specced to reuse — performs a WRITE (POST mint, DELETE stale placeholders) and its own doc-comment (inviteData.ts:363-364) says it runs 'on the caller's OWN person, under the caller's own JWT.' Nothing in this thread or the probe establishes whether an admin can invoke mint/DELETE against ANOTHER member's person — only that she can READ it. [speculative] the same inheritance mechanism that makes reads work (entity-level _editor inherited from the database root, per '_inheritrights:true' at inviteData.ts:201) probably also authorizes writes, but this is an inference, not an observation, and it is the same class of inference (prop-def → behavior) that was wrong once already on this exact issue (the dropped inverted-marker premise). Worth a probe before RED, same shape as the read probe.

(ii) No shared roster-row read of person.entu_user exists yet. listActiveMembers (rosterData.ts) fetches only person,_parent. The only existing three-state discriminator is listLinkedIdentities (linkedIdentities.ts:46-79, main) — generic over any personId, already does exactly the uid-vs-invite-vs-absent split needed (returns identities[] + pendingInvites count) — but its only current caller passes the CALLER's OWN personId (routes/profile/+page.svelte:328). Reusing it per roster row (e.g. fanned out with Promise.all, matching the existing profile fan-out pattern the module's header comment already documents) is the natural design but is not yet decided/built.

(iii) 'withdraw' (sweep-without-mint) does not exist as a separable function. mintSelfLinkInvite couples sweep+mint in one function body (inviteData.ts:371-461); building withdraw needs either a refactor to extract the sweep as its own exported function reused by both, or a near-duplicate. A build-shape choice, not a product one.

(iv) No fixture path exists for the 'missing'/'absent' state. Since createInvite can never produce it (see finding 2 above), RED-phase tests (and any live polyphony verification) need a way to construct a person with no entu_user key attached to a real member — outside the app's own create path. Needs a seed/script decision before Tallis can write a red test for that state.

(v) File-overlap sequencing with the live #287 pipeline (both touch roster/+page.svelte) — already ruled to be team-lead's (not PO's) call per Mihkel's correction comment; flagged here only as a live constraint, not a question to route anywhere.

(vi) UI copy ('kutsu' / 'saada uuesti' / 'tühista kutse') — 'kutsu' has precedent (messages/et.json:59, 'Kutsu uus liige', for the existing create-new-invite flow); 'saada uuesti' and 'tühista kutse' do not exist anywhere in main at HEAD (git grep, zero hits) — net-new copy proposed by Gama in-thread, not yet authored. Normal Comenius-lane work, not a blocking ambiguity.

findings.title: 4. Where the body's claims stand against code at HEAD
findings.detail:
No code-level contradiction found: every source citation in the body checks out verbatim against main at HEAD — rosterData.ts:118-127 throw (matches, confirmed at lines 118/123-126), createInvite's person→editor-grant→member sequence (inviteData.ts:166 onward, matches), linkedIdentities.ts:37's exact quoted comment (matches verbatim).

The one claim that is now WRONG, but is a live-behavior claim, not a code claim: 'entu_user is _sharing: private, and linkedIdentities reads the caller's OWN person... An admin cannot read another member's redemption state today.' The prop-def fact (_sharing: private) and the doc-comment fact (function is documented/used for 'own' reads) are both still accurate in the code as written — nothing in the CODE asserts or denies cross-person read access; that was an INFERENCE from those two facts, and the inference was disproved by the live probe, not by anything in the codebase. Worth flagging precisely because it's the same failure mode almost repeated with the inverted-marker design later in the same thread (design built on an unobserved premise) — the thread caught it both times, but a reader skimming just the body would still take '#2, admin cannot read' at face value.
